summary: Kestrel Pay's manual load is concentrated in three places: repetitive payout-status questions, onboarding intake rework, and false-positive compliance alerts. The fastest, lowest-risk wins are grounded self-service for payout status and a completeness pre-check on applications. The largest pool of hours sits in sanctions and monitoring alerts, but those are regulated decisions, so the recommendation is AI-prepared case files with analyst sign-off, phased in after controls are agreed with the MLRO.

opportunities.title: Grounded payout-status answers in chat and agent assist
opportunities.problem: About 30% of tickets ask where a payout is. The answer already exists in the settlement dashboard; agents look it up and paste it into a macro.
opportunities.proposed_solution: Answer payout and FX-rate questions from the merchant's own settlement records via in-app chat and WhatsApp, citing the payout reference and expected date. Unresolved or unusual cases hand off to an agent with the lookup already done.
opportunities.human_role: Agents handle anything the record cannot explain (missing payouts, partner delays) and own customer-facing exceptions.
opportunities.feasibility_rationale: Data is structured and already in the settlement system; answer templates exist.
opportunities.risk_rationale: Wrong ETA is an annoyance, not a regulatory issue. The 2024 chatbot failed because it was not grounded in merchant data, which this design addresses.

evidence.why: Agent copies ETA from dashboard into reply
Same lookup-and-paste pattern
Support lead: a third of the queue, answer is in the dashboard
Past chatbot failed because it could not see payout status

open_questions: Does the settlement system expose a per-merchant API we can query in real time?

opportunities.title: Application completeness pre-check at submission
opportunities.problem: Associates read every application against 23 fields and 4 documents; about 28% bounce back, which also generates document-resubmission tickets.
opportunities.proposed_solution: Check fields and classify uploaded documents at the moment of submission (right document in the right slot, legible, not expired) and tell the merchant immediately what is missing.
opportunities.human_role: Associates review only flagged applications. Compliance judgments are unchanged.
opportunities.feasibility_rationale: Field checks are rules; document classification and legibility checks are mature.
opportunities.risk_rationale: Pre-check only gates completeness, not eligibility. Errors send a merchant back to upload again, which is the current outcome anyway.

evidence.why: 12 min per application, 28% rework rate
Agent requests re-upload of unreadable ID
Onboarding manager: biggest drag is the first step
SOP defines 23 fields and 4 documents to check

opportunities.title: Onboarding emails and go-live checklist from API logs
opportunities.problem: The sandbox welcome email is identical every time, and most of the 15-item go-live checklist can be confirmed from the merchant's own API activity.
opportunities.proposed_solution: Trigger the welcome email automatically when keys are issued, and pre-fill the go-live checklist from API logs so the call covers only the items that are not yet green.
opportunities.human_role: Account managers keep the call for strategic merchants and anything red on the checklist.
opportunities.feasibility_rationale: Template and log data already exist.
opportunities.risk_rationale: Low exposure: worst case is an unnecessary call.

evidence.why: Same welcome email sent each time
30-minute call walking a 15-item checklist
Checklist items are confirmable from API logs
SOP: provision keys, send WEL-02, schedule go-live call

opportunities.title: Developer-support answers grounded in API docs and request logs
opportunities.problem: API tickets repeat (live keys in sandbox, failing webhooks) and the docs already answer most of them.
opportunities.proposed_solution: Classify incoming developer tickets, check the merchant's recent API errors, and draft a reply that links the exact docs section. Simple cases are answered directly.
opportunities.human_role: Solutions engineers handle anything involving idempotency, money movement or custom builds.
opportunities.feasibility_rationale: Docs and error logs are structured; error classes are few.
opportunities.risk_rationale: Technical guidance only; no money movement.

evidence.why: Live-key-in-sandbox ticket, 'same issue as many others'
Webhook endpoint returning 500
Docs answer most API tickets, developers miss the page

opportunities.title: Settlement reconciliation auto-matching with explanations
opportunities.problem: Each mismatch ticket means exporting three reports and matching in Excel; about a third still escalate to finance ops.
opportunities.proposed_solution: Match ledger, partner-bank and processor records automatically, and have the model explain the remaining breaks in plain language (timing, FX, missing batch) for the agent to send.
opportunities.human_role: Finance ops resolves true breaks and signs off any balance adjustment.
opportunities.feasibility_rationale: Matching logic is deterministic, but needs reliable report feeds from partners.
opportunities.risk_rationale: A wrong explanation to a merchant about money is a trust issue; adjustments stay manual.

evidence.why: Agent exports three reports and matches in Excel
Missing transactions rebuilt from ledger export
Support lead: most-dreaded ticket, up to an hour each

open_questions: Are partner-bank statements available by API or only as portal downloads?

opportunities.title: Registry lookup and bank-account name matching
opportunities.problem: Associates type registration numbers into the government portal and compare results to certificates by eye; name-on-account mismatches cause email back-and-forth.
opportunities.proposed_solution: Extract fields from the certificate, query the registry, and show a side-by-side match report with discrepancies highlighted. Fuzzy-match bank account names and draft the clarification email when needed.
opportunities.human_role: Associate confirms the match report; discrepancies go to a compliance analyst as today.
opportunities.feasibility_rationale: Registry access method is uncertain; extraction itself is mature.
opportunities.risk_rationale: A false match creates exposure, so every result is human-confirmed.

evidence.why: 18 min per application, 22% rework
Name-on-account mismatches resolved by email
Mechanical, but a wrong match creates exposure
SOP requires registry confirmation

open_questions: Does the registry offer an API or bulk lookup, or only a web portal?

opportunities.title: Transaction-monitoring and KYC-refresh rationale drafting
opportunities.problem: Most monitoring alerts are known seasonal patterns; the real cost is writing an audit-ready rationale for each one.
opportunities.proposed_solution: Pull 90 days of merchant history, prior alerts and invoices into a case summary and draft the closing rationale for the analyst to edit and sign.
opportunities.human_role: The analyst decides every alert outcome and signs the rationale. Escalations to the MLRO are unchanged.
opportunities.feasibility_rationale: Inputs are structured; drafting from them is a strong LLM use case.
opportunities.risk_rationale: Regulated record; mitigated by mandatory analyst sign-off and an audit trail of edits.

evidence.why: Rationale written for a closed alert
90 days of activity reviewed manually
Real cost is writing rationale that survives audit
AI may prepare the case file, not close alerts

opportunities.title: Sanctions name-match case preparation
opportunities.problem: Over 90% of name-match alerts are false positives; analysts re-check DOB and country fields the system already holds.
opportunities.proposed_solution: For each alert, assemble the list entry and the customer's verified identity data side by side, highlight differing fields, and pre-draft the disposition note. The analyst makes and records the decision.
opportunities.human_role: A named analyst clears or escalates every alert. No alert is closed by software.
opportunities.feasibility_rationale: Field comparison is simple; the work is integration and controls.
opportunities.risk_rationale: Sanctions decisions carry regulatory liability; requires MLRO-agreed controls, sampling QA and a data processing agreement for any AI vendor.

evidence.why: Cleared after manual DOB and nationality comparison
Fuzzy match on a different country and registration
More than nine in ten alerts are false positives
Must stay with a named analyst
Personal data only to approved processors
Partial matches cleared by analyst with recorded rationale

open_questions: Will the MLRO accept AI-prepared case files, and what QA sampling rate?

opportunities.title: Chargeback evidence pack assembly
opportunities.problem: Agents chase merchants for evidence over several emails and write each dispute narrative by hand under strict scheme deadlines.
opportunities.proposed_solution: Send the merchant a structured evidence request on day one, collect uploads in one place, and draft the dispute narrative from order, delivery and device data.
opportunities.human_role: Agents review and submit every dispute to the scheme portal.
opportunities.risk_rationale: Missed deadlines or weak narratives lose money; human submits.

evidence.why: Evidence gathered over four emails
Narrative written manually from logs
Strict scheme deadlines
